ui.searchPrompt: Ask a question, e.g. "insert a table"…
ui.intro: Type what you want to do in the box above, or just answer the questions below.
ui.noMatch: I couldn't match your words, so let's find it step by step.

q_root.question: Do you want to write a mathematical formula or symbol?

q_math.question: Is it a fraction (one value over another)?

q_math2.question: Is it an exponent or a subscript (like x² or xᵢ)?

q_math5.question: Is it a sum (Σ), an integral (∫) or a product (Π)?

q_math7.question: Is it a special symbol (Greek letter, ≤, ∞, ℝ…)?

q_table1.question: Do you want to create a new table?

q_table2.question: Do you want to change the number of rows or columns?

q_table3.question: Do you want to merge or split cells?

q_table4.question: Do you want to resize rows or columns?

q_draw.question: Is it about a shape, an arrow or an image?

q_image.question: Do you want to add an image to the page?

q_arrow.question: Do you want to create a new arrow?

q_shape.question: Do you want to create a new shape (circle, square, triangle)?

q_text2.question: Do you want to align a paragraph (left, center, right, justify)?

q_code1.question: Do you want to write a code block?

q_code2.question: Do you want to run a code block?

q_file2.question: Do you want to open an existing document?

cmd_general.title: How typing commands works
body: Many things are created by typing a command: a backslash (\), the command name, then Space.
> \pi  then Space  →  π
- Math: \a/b, \x^2, \x_i, \sqrt(x), \matrix(1,2;3,4), \sum, \int, \prod, \lim and symbols like \pi or \<=
- Objects: \circle, \square, \triangle, \arrow and \tab (table)
- Press Backspace right after a conversion to get the raw command back and edit it.
- To write a real backslash, type it twice (\\).
captions: Type a backslash and a command name…
…then press Space: the command is converted.
Press Backspace right after to get the raw command back and edit it.

math_fraction.title: Insert a fraction
body: Type a backslash, the numerator, a slash and the denominator, then press Space:
> \a/b
- Each side is a word or number, or anything inside parentheses, which may itself contain math: \(a+b)/(c^2), \1/(1/x).
- Example: \3/4 gives 3 over 4.
- Press Backspace right after the conversion to edit the raw command.

math_power.title: Insert an exponent (power)
body: Type a backslash, the base, ^ and the exponent, then press Space:
- The base is made of letters and digits.
- The exponent is a single word or number, or anything inside parentheses.
- Use parentheses for longer exponents, e.g. \e^(-x).
- Math can be nested inside parentheses: \x^(1/2), \(a/b)^2, \sqrt(x^2/y_1), \sum_(i=1)^(n)(i^2/2). Parentheses around the base stay visible.

math_subscript.title: Insert a subscript
body: Type a backslash, the base, _ and the subscript, then press Space:
> \x_i
- The base is made of letters and digits.
- The subscript is a single word or number, or anything inside parentheses.

math_sqrt.title: Insert a square root
body: Type a backslash, sqrt, then the content in parentheses, and press Space:
> \sqrt(x+1)
- Anything between the parentheses goes under the root sign.

math_matrix.title: Insert a matrix
body: Type a backslash, matrix, then the values in parentheses, and press Space:
- Separate the columns with commas and the rows with semicolons.
- The example gives a 2×2 matrix drawn with brackets.

math_sum.title: Insert a sum (Σ)
body: Type a backslash, sum, then the expression in parentheses, and press Space:
> \sum(i)
To add bounds, give the lower bound, then ^ and the upper bound, then the expression:
- A bound is either a single word (\sum_1^n(i)) or anything in parentheses.
- The expression always goes in parentheses.

math_integral.title: Insert an integral (∫)
body: Type a backslash, int, then the expression in parentheses, and press Space:
> \int(x)
To add bounds, give the lower bound, then ^ and the upper bound, then the expression:
- A bound is either a single word or anything in parentheses, e.g. \int_(-1)^(1)(x).
- The expression always goes in parentheses.

math_product.title: Insert a product (Π)
body: Type a backslash, prod, then the expression in parentheses, and press Space:
> \prod(i)
To add bounds:
- A bound is either a single word or anything in parentheses.
- The expression always goes in parentheses.

math_limit.title: Insert a limit
body: Type a backslash, lim, then the expression in parentheses, and press Space:
> \lim(x)
To show what the variable tends to:
> \lim_(x->infinity)(1/x)
- Write -> for the arrow. The word infinity becomes ∞.
- The condition and the expression both go in parentheses.

math_symbols.title: Insert a math symbol
body: Type a backslash and the symbol name, then press Space:
- Greek letters: \pi \alpha \beta \theta \lambda \phi \psi \delta
- Operators: \pm (±)  \times (×)  \inf or \infinity (∞)
- Number sets: \NN (ℕ)  \ZZ (ℤ)  \QQ (ℚ)  \RR (ℝ)  \CC (ℂ)  \PP (ℙ)  \HH (ℍ)
captions: Type \ and the symbol name, then Space.
The symbol is inserted as text.

shape_insert.title: Insert a shape
body: Type one of these commands, then press Space:
> \circle
> \square
> \triangle
The shape appears in the middle of the page. Then you can:
- Click it to select it, drag it to move it.
- Drag the blue square at its corner to resize it (hold Ctrl to keep the proportions).
- Drag the green dot above it to rotate it (hold Ctrl to snap to 15° steps).
- Right-click it for fill color and opacity, border color, opacity and thickness, and layer order.
- Select it and press Delete to remove it.
captions: The shape appears in the middle of the page.

shape_edit.title: Move, resize and style a shape
body: - Click the shape to select it. Drag it to move it.
- Blue square at the corner: drag to resize (hold Ctrl to keep the proportions).
- Green dot above: drag to rotate (hold Ctrl to snap to 15° steps).
- Right-click: fill color and opacity, border color, opacity and thickness (0 = no border).
- Right-click also lets you move the shape forward or back one level.
- Select it and press Delete (or Backspace) to remove it.
- Hold Alt while dragging to turn off the alignment guides.
captions: Drag the blue square to resize (Ctrl keeps proportions).
Drag the green dot to rotate (Ctrl snaps to 15°).
Drag the shape itself to move it.

arrow_insert.title: Insert an arrow
body: Type this command, then press Space:
> \arrow
A straight arrow appears on the page. Then you can:
- Drag the blue dots at its ends to move the start or the end.
- Drag the green dot in the middle to curve the arrow.
- Drag the line itself to move the whole arrow.
- Right-click for color, opacity and thickness, and layer order.
- Select it and press Delete to remove it.
captions: An arrow appears. Drag its dots to adjust it.

arrow_edit.title: Move, curve and style an arrow
body: - Click the arrow to select it. Drag the line to move the whole arrow.
- Blue dots: drag to move the start or the end.
- Green dot: drag to curve the arrow.
- Right-click: color, opacity (0-100) and thickness (1-20), plus layer order.
- Select it and press Delete (or Backspace) to remove it.
captions: Drag the blue dots to move the ends, the green dot to curve it.

table_insert.title: Insert a table
body: Type this command, then press Space:
> \tab
A 2×2 table appears (up to 20 rows × 20 columns). Then you can:
- Click a cell and type. Cells support formatting and \ commands too.
- Change the number of rows and columns: right-click the table, type a number in Rows or Columns and press Enter.
- Merge cells: drag across several cells to select them, right-click, then Merge cells. Right-click a merged cell and choose Split cells to undo.
- Resize: drag a divider between cells. Hold Ctrl while dragging to move a single divider, and Alt to turn off snapping.
- Move the table: drag the blue square at its top-left corner.
- Delete it: select the table (click its border or the blue square) and press Delete.
- Right-click also has layer options (move forward / back one level).
captions: A 2×2 table appears. Click a cell and type.

table_rows_cols.title: Change the number of rows and columns
body: - Right-click the table (not on selected text).
- Type a number in Rows (1-20) and/or Columns (1-20), then press Enter.
- Extra rows and columns are added at the end; removing them deletes the last ones and their content.
- Merges that no longer fit are removed.
captions: Right-click the table: set Rows and Columns (1-20), then press Enter.

table_merge.title: Merge and split table cells
body: - Drag across several cells to select them (they turn blue).
- Right-click and choose Merge cells. The text of the merged cells is combined.
- To undo: right-click the merged cell and choose Split cells.
- Merged cells can still be resized with the dividers.
captions: Drag across several cells to select them.
Right-click a merged cell and choose Split cells to undo.

table_resize.title: Resize table rows and columns
body: - Drag a divider between two columns or rows to resize them.
- Hold Ctrl while dragging to move a single divider (only that part of the border).
- Hold Alt to turn off snapping to nearby objects.
- Rows grow automatically when the text inside needs more room.
captions: Drag a divider to resize a column or a row.
Ctrl+drag moves a single divider. Alt turns off snapping.

table_move_delete.title: Move or delete a table
body: - Move: drag the blue square at the top-left corner of the table.
- Delete: select the table (click its border or the blue square) and press Delete.
- Right-click the table to bring it forward or send it back one level.
captions: Drag the blue square (top-left corner) to move the table.
Select the table and press Delete to remove it.

image_import.title: Import an image
body: - Right-click an empty area of the page (with no text selected).
- Choose Import an image and pick a file.
- The image is placed on the page. Click it to move it; the blue square resizes it and the green dot rotates it.
- Right-click the image for opacity and layer order. Select it and press Delete to remove it.
captions: Right-click an empty area of the page.
Pick a file: the image is inserted on the page.

image_edit.title: Move, resize and rotate an image
body: - Click the image to select it. Drag it to move it.
- Blue square at the corner: drag to resize (hold Ctrl to keep the proportions).
- Green dot above: drag to rotate (hold Ctrl to snap to 15° steps).
- Right-click: opacity (0-100) and layer order.
- Hold Alt while dragging to turn off the alignment guides.
captions: Click the image to select it. Drag it to move it.
Blue square: resize (Ctrl keeps proportions). Green dot: rotate.

text_format.title: Format text (bold, size, color…)
body: Select the text, then right-click it. The menu offers:
- Size: pick a preset or type your own (1-400) and press Enter.
- Color.
- Bold, Italic, Strikethrough.
- Underline, Dotted underline and Underline color.
- Highlight and Highlight color.
- Alignment (see the alignment topic).
captions: Also available: dotted underline, underline color and highlight color.

text_align.title: Align a paragraph
body: - Select the text of the paragraph (or click in it), then right-click.
- Open Alignment and choose Align left, Center, Align right or Justify.
- Alignment is not available inside code blocks.
- It works in table cells and text boxes too.
captions: Select the paragraph, right-click and open Alignment.

text_link.title: Add a link
body: - Type or paste an address starting with http:// or https://.
- It is turned into a link automatically (trailing punctuation is left out).
- Ctrl+click (Cmd+click on Mac) opens the link in your browser.
- Links are not detected inside code blocks.
captions: Type or paste an address starting with http:// or https://
It turns into a link automatically.

text_move.title: Move text anywhere on the page
body: - Select the text you want to move: a blue handle appears at the top-left corner of the selection.
- Drag that handle: the text becomes a free text box, placed where you drop it.
- The original place is left blank, so the rest of the text does not move.
- See the text box topic to edit, resize and style it.
captions: Select some text: a blue handle appears at its top-left corner.
Drag the handle: the text becomes a free text box.
The text box can be placed anywhere on the page.

textbox_edit.title: Edit and style a text box
body: - Click the box to select it and drag it to move it (or use the blue square at its top-left corner).
- Double-click to edit the text inside; press Escape to stop editing.
- Drag the blue handle on the right edge to change the width. The height follows the text.
- Right-click: Border visible and Border color, Background visible and Background color (its opacity follows the color picker), plus layer order.
- Select text inside and right-click for the usual text formatting.
- Select the box and press Delete to remove it. An empty box disappears by itself.
captions: Drag a text box to move it; double-click to edit its text.
Drag the blue handle on the right to change its width.

layers.title: Bring objects forward or send them back
body: Shapes, arrows, images, tables and text boxes are stacked in layers.
- Right-click an object and choose Move forward one level or Move back one level.
- Each click moves it one step in the stack.
captions: Overlapping objects are stacked in layers.
Right-click an object: move it forward or back one level.

snap_guides.title: Alignment guides (snapping)
body: - While you move or resize an object, pink guides appear when it lines up with the page edges, the page center or another object.
- The object snaps to the guide when it is close.
- Hold Alt while dragging to turn off snapping.
captions: While moving or resizing, pink guides show alignment with the page and other objects.
Hold Alt to turn off snapping.

code_block.title: Write a code block
body: Start a line with three backticks and the language, write your code, and close with three backticks:
> ```python
> print("Hello")
- The block gets a code background and syntax highlighting.
- Highlighted languages: Java, Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, C, C++, C#, HTML/XML, CSS, JSON, SQL, Bash, OCaml. Others get generic highlighting.
- The fence lines are dimmed when your cursor is outside the block.
- The color theme is chosen in Settings.
- You can run some languages: right-click inside the block (see the run topic).
captions: Type three backticks followed by the language (python, java, js, c, sql…).
Write your code, then close the block with three backticks.
The block is styled and syntax-highlighted.

code_run.title: Run a code block
body: - Right-click inside a code block and choose Run code.
- Runnable languages: Python, JavaScript, Bash, Java, OCaml and C (the interpreter or compiler must be installed and in your PATH).
- The first time, a confirmation asks you to trust the code: it runs on your computer with the app's rights.
- The output appears under the block. Use ■ to stop, ▾ to collapse and ✕ to close.
- A run is stopped after 10 seconds, and the output is limited to 20,000 characters.
captions: First time only: confirm that you trust the code.
The output appears under the block. Stop (■) or close (✕) it from there.

code_theme.title: Change the code block theme
body: - Click the Settings button.
- Choose a theme in Code block theme.
- All code blocks update immediately.
captions: Open Settings and choose the code block theme.

file_save.title: Save your document
body: - Press Ctrl+S (Cmd+S on Mac) or click the Save button.
- The first time, you choose a file name; after that, it saves to the same file.
- Documents are saved as .docx files. TypO stores extra data in them, so reopening a file in TypO restores every object (tables, shapes, arrows, text boxes, images).
captions: The first time, you choose a file name; after that it saves to the same file.

file_open.title: Open a document
body: - Click the Open button and choose a .docx file.
- Only .docx files can be opened.
- Documents saved by TypO come back with all their objects, margins and page settings.

file_saveas.title: Save as .docx or export to PDF
body: - Click the Save As button and choose a name and a type.
- Word document (.docx): can be reopened in TypO and opened in Word.
- PDF: a picture of each page. It cannot be reopened for editing, and code output panels are not included.
- After a .docx Save As, Ctrl+S saves to that file.

page_new.title: Add a page
body: - Click the New Page button to add a blank page at the end.
- A new page is also created automatically when your text no longer fits on the page.
- New pages follow the margins and page numbering set in Settings.
captions: Click New Page to add a blank page.
A page is also added automatically when the text overflows.

page_manage.title: Delete a page or change its orientation
body: - Right-click an empty area of the page (with no text selected).
- Toggle Orientation (Portrait/Landscape) switches that page.
- Delete Page removes it; the remaining pages are renumbered.
- Import an image is in the same menu.
captions: Right-click an empty area of the page.

view_navigate.title: Zoom and move around
body: - Zoom: Ctrl + mouse wheel (from 0.8× to 3×).
- Move up and down: mouse wheel or the vertical scrollbar.
- Move left and right: Shift + mouse wheel or the horizontal scrollbar.
captions: Ctrl + mouse wheel: zoom in or out.
Mouse wheel: move up and down.
Shift + mouse wheel: move left and right.

settings_margins.title: Change the page margins
body: - Click the Settings button and open Margins (cm).
- Type a value in centimeters for Left, Top, Right or Bottom, then press Enter.
- Tick Link all four to apply the same margin to the four sides.
- Left + Right and Top + Bottom must each stay within 19 cm. A field turns red when the value is not valid.
captions: Type a value in cm for Left, Top, Right or Bottom and press Enter.
Link all four applies the same margin to the four sides.

settings_page_numbers.title: Show page numbers
body: - Click the Settings button.
- Tick Number the pages.
- The number appears at the bottom of each page, in the document and in the exports.
captions: Click Settings and tick Number the pages.

settings_colors.title: Change colors and appearance
body: - Click the Settings button.
- Background color: the color behind the pages.
- App theme: the colors of the whole app (selection included). Import… loads your own theme file (.json).
- Code block theme: the look of code blocks.
- Number the pages and Margins (cm) are in the same menu.

not_found.title: I couldn't pinpoint it
body: Sorry, I couldn't work out what you are looking for.
- Use the Back button and answer differently, or use I don't know.
- Try the search box with other words (for example: table, fraction, bold, zoom).
- Commands typed with a backslash are explained in 'How typing commands works'.
